about.challenge: Challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots
about.p1: Satellites have recorded fires since 2000, but the newer VIIRS sensors see far more small fires than MODIS, so raw records jump when VIIRS arrives.
about.p2: With Suomi-NPP ended and MODIS retiring, 25 years of fire history risks becoming incomparable with the satellites that continue.
about.p3: FireRings harmonizes both into one record with honest uncertainty, and turns it into a calendar anyone can read, hear or print.

help.calendar: The calendar shows one square per month: rows are years (newest on top), columns are months. Brighter = more fire.

help.modes: The sensor switch shows harmonized values or each satellite's raw counts. Raw counts jump when VIIRS starts; harmonized values do not.

help.status: Status compares a month with the same month in all past years: ▼ below normal, ● near normal, ▲ above normal, ⚠ extreme.

hs.title: Hotspots
m.ai_note: All statistics are computed by tested code in src/compute; no AI model computes any number shown here.
m.cov_x: Share of test months inside the 90% band — near 90% means honest intervals.
m.dl_coef_x: Effective harmonized ÷ raw ratios per calendar month over the overlap, derived from the published series.
m.l1: Satellites see a fire only when they pass overhead and clouds or smoke allow; small or short fires are missed, more often by MODIS.
m.l2: A hotspot is a hot pixel, not a fire: one big fire can light many cells, and many small fires can share one.
m.l3: Before {viirs} the record rests on MODIS alone, so uncertainty is wider and small fires are under-counted.
m.l4: Custom drawn areas sum whole {km} km cells, so their edges are approximate.
m.l5: The current month stays partial until it ends; it is not ranked.
m.l6: This build shows synthetic demo data: it shows how the app works, not what happened.
m.mae_x: Typical monthly miss on the test years, in hotspots.
m.p_onset_v: Cumulative activity passes 10% of a typical season
m.p_rule_v: One cell-day counts once, however many detections.
m.s1_b: Keep vegetation-fire detections that pass the confidence filter; drop static industrial heat sources.
m.s2_b: Every detection goes onto one {km} km grid. One cell-day counts once, however many detections.
m.s3_b: Where MODIS and VIIRS both observed ({overlap}), learn how their counts relate, month by month.
m.s4_b: Express the whole record in one sensor-agnostic unit, with wider uncertainty in the MODIS-only years.
m.seam: The sensor seam, before and after

m.why: Suomi-NPP data delivery ended on 1 November 2026 and MODIS is being retired. Without harmonization, 25 years of fire history stops being comparable with the satellites that continue (NOAA-20, NOAA-21).
